two real steps: the identity 1 - sin^2 = cos^2 collapses the sum to 2 sec t, and only then does cos t = 1/2 give t = 60 from the table. Unlike the pure proofs nearby this one ends in an angle

square the given difference, extract 2 sin cos, feed it into the sum of squares; the Pythagorean identity is used twice on a supplied relation
